conditions: Concurrent real traffic on the same physical interface; fresh, separate SQLite databases.
Identical local City and ASN database contents; no frontend subscribers attached to either measured collector.
No deliberate traffic generation; existing host applications and the installed monitor continued running.
Both collectors ran as the same normal user with CAP_NET_RAW only. eBPF was disabled in both fresh configurations.
Default background checks remained enabled; no on-demand Frida/deep inspections, model requests or firewall policy were configured.
Capture defaults differ: Rust uses non-promiscuous mode, a 4096-byte snapshot and an ip-or-ip6-or-arp filter; Python uses promiscuous mode, a 65535-byte snapshot and an ip-or-ip6 filter.
CPU includes all threads in each collector process; 100% means one logical core. RSS includes resident file mappings.
Original Python exposes parser and queue drop counts, but not libpcap kernel drop counters.
This is one five-minute workload, not a feature-parity, full-desktop, long-term stability or maximum-throughput benchmark.
